S36.01.needs: a Free or paid account with web search available for the chat
S36.01.note: The marker is drawn in MarkdownInline.tsx (CitationMarker), not MessageBubble.tsx:1972 as the plan says; whether the model writes a marker is up to the answer, and I did not confirm the on-screen control that turns web search on.
steps: Sign in and start a new chat on the first screen.
Ask a question that needs current web information, such as recent news on a topic.
Wait for the answer to finish streaming.
Look for teal bracket markers like [1] or [2] inside the answer text.
Tap a marker: a dialog opens with the source title, publisher and buttons Cancel and Open page.
Compare with Expected: each marker should point to the source for the claim next to it.
S36.01.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that needs current web facts > read the answer > find the small teal bracket markers such as [1] placed after claims > tap one

S36.02.needs: a chat answer that used web search, so the answer has cited sources
S36.02.note: The sheet shows the title on each row; the Sources pill is hidden for research reports, which use a separate list instead.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Under the answer, tap the pill whose text is Sources.
In the sheet titled Sources, read the bold line of each row.
Compare with Expected: each cited source should show its title.
S36.02.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the rows in the sheet

S36.03.needs: a chat answer that used web search
S36.03.note: The publisher is shown as a domain taken from the URL, not a publisher name, unless the source supplies one.
steps: Open a web-search answer and tap the Sources pill under it.
Look at the small grey first line of each row.
Compare with Expected: each row should show the site domain, for example the publisher name, before the title.
S36.03.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the small grey first line of each row

S36.04.needs: a chat answer that used web search and a network connection
S36.04.note: The web address itself is not printed on screen; the row only shows an accessibility hint, Opens in the in-app browser. Tapping a marker also offers Open page.
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Tap a source row that has a web address.
Watch for the in-app browser to open the source page.
Compare with Expected: the source opens. A row with no valid web address is not tappable.
S36.04.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > tap a source row

S36.05.needs: a chat answer that used web search, where the source reports a publication date
S36.05.note: If the source has no date, no date appears; this is the expected behaviour in code.
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Read the grey first line of a row: it shows the publisher then a date after a dot.
Tap a bracket marker in the answer and read the dialog body for a line that starts with Published.
Compare with Expected: the date shows when the source has one, and no date is shown when it is unknown.
S36.05.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the grey first line of a row, or tap a bracket marker and read the dialog

S36.06.needs: a chat answer with a source that has a retrieval time; for the report path, a saved research report
S36.06.note: The retrieval date is shown once for the whole report, not per source, and the chat Sources sheet does not show it; how the side drawer is opened was not confirmed in the code.
steps: In a chat answer with web search, tap a bracket marker such as [1].
Read the dialog body for a line that starts with Retrieved followed by a date.
Optionally open the side drawer, tap Reports, open a saved report, and scroll to the end.
Compare with Expected: the report shows the line Sources retrieved with a date.
S36.06.where: Tap a bracket marker in a web-search answer and read the dialog for a line starting with Retrieved; or open the side drawer > Reports > open a saved report > scroll to the bottom

S36.07.needs: a chat answer that used web search; for the file icon, a project with a file that a chat cites
S36.07.note: Web sources do not get a type icon: the square mark shows a letter for the site, and the Globe icon shows only in the search result cards. File and past-chat citations have their own chips with icons; I did not confirm a path to open a project chat.
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Look at the square mark at the left of each row: it holds the first letter of the site and has a Globe icon beside the domain in the search result cards.
Open a chat that cites a project file, if you have one, and look for the file icon on its citation chip.
Compare with Expected: web sources, file sources and chat sources should each show an icon for their type.
S36.07.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > look at the mark at the left of each row

S36.08.needs: a chat answer that used web search and whose sources include snippets
S36.08.note: The app shows the source snippet; it does not check that the snippet is the sentence that supports the claim, so the tester should judge that.
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Read the smaller text under each row title, which is up to three lines.
Tap a bracket marker and read the body text of the dialog.
Compare with Expected: the excerpt shown should be the text that supports the claim.
S36.08.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > read the grey text under a row title, or tap a bracket marker and read the dialog body

S36.16.needs: a chat answer that used web search with several sources
S36.16.note: Where a marker lands depends on the model's text; the code only moves markers next to their links, so placement is judged by the tester.
steps: Ask a question that uses web search and wait for the answer.
Find a sentence with a teal bracket marker such as [1] right after it.
Tap the marker: the dialog names the source for that marker.
If a marker has several numbers, tap it and pick one entry from the list, which has the button Dismiss sources.
Compare with Expected: each marker should sit at the claim that its source supports.
S36.16.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > read the answer and compare each bracket marker with the sentence before it

S36.19.needs: a chat answer with a source that has no valid web address, which is rare, so the tester may not find one
S36.19.note: On mobile there is no text saying a source was not captured; an uncaptured source row is only greyed out and not tappable. The uncaptured-source notice exists only on web in apps/web/features/chat/components/research/ResearchReportView.tsx, using the key counts.uncapturedSources, which mobile does not use.
steps: Open the Sources sheet under a web-search answer.
Look for a row without an external-link arrow at its right; such a row cannot be tapped.
Tap a bracket marker whose source cannot open; if the open fails, a dialog titled Could not open citation appears.
Compare with Expected: the product should say the source cannot be opened, not show a dead link.
S36.19.where: First screen after sign-in > start a chat > ask a question that uses web search > under the answer tap the Sources pill > look at a source row that has no web address
